prompts:
Photograph of a sturdy English merchant ship of about 1620 with a broad,
deep hull, a raised wooden stern two decks high, its poop and
quarterdeck planked like the rest of the hull, and a smaller raised bow
deck: square course and topsail on the fore and main masts, a lateen
sail on the mizzen, a square spritsail under the steeply raked bowsprit,
weathered buff and black paint, simple trim and a few small gun ports,
under sail, seen from above at an angle. It floats on the water, its
hull cut at the waterline. Plain flat blue background. Historical
reenactment photography, sharp focus, realistic. The whole ship is built
of planked wood: no tower, nothing of stone.
